issues: Statistic: "seventy out of every hundred people work in farming" is the book's figure; today agriculture employs a smaller share of Pakistan's workforce (roughly 37–40%), though most rural households depend on it. Kept as printed. The proverb "خپله لاسه ګُله لاسه" is transcribed as printed; its literal translation is SpaceBook's.
History: "when Pakistan was made there were no industries here" is a simplification; there was very little industry in 1947. Kept as printed.

Hadith: the saying "الکاسب حبیب اللہ" (the earner is the friend of Allah) is widely quoted, but hadith scholars do not consider it authentic as a saying of the Prophet ﷺ. It is transcribed as printed.

decorative: An old engraving of Jabir ibn Hayyan, a bearded man in a robe, holding up a glass flask beside laboratory vessels.
issues: Layout: the last line on this page runs under the picture and continues on the next page; a word or two between "علمي ماحول وهٔ" and "چې په جابر" is hidden at the picture edge.

Spelling: the book prints "CRYSTALIZATION"; the usual spelling is "crystallisation/crystallization". Kept as printed. History: Jabir's birthplace (Tus/Khorasan) and the story of his father's execution are traditional accounts; the corpus attributed to him is debated by historians.

Science: "plastic" (پلاسټک) did not exist in Jabir's time; the book probably means waxed or oil-proofed cloth (موم جامه). Jabir's death date is given variously (c. 806–816 CE); the book's 814 CE is kept. Calx weighing more than the metal is a later observation; attributing it to Jabir is the book's claim.
Exercise 9, item 4: "لویه" (feminine) does not agree with "سائنسدان" (masculine); the lesson itself uses "لویه کارنامه" and "لوے سائنسدان". The intended pair is given with a note.

issues: History: Ibn Sina's given name is usually recorded as al-Husayn (Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Abd Allah ibn Sina); his birthplace is Afshana near Bukhara (c. 980 CE). Kept as printed.
Names: the book prints "ابوعبیده جرجاني" and "کوویه"; historians give Abu Ubayd al-Juzjani and Kakuya (Kakuyid). Kept as printed in the Pashto.
History: Ibn Sina died in Hamadan, and his mausoleum is in Hamadan, not Isfahan as the book says. Kept as printed.
